Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we keep momentum on the FinApps integration: 

Recap (what we covered)

Hi James —

Thanks — good questions. Short answers here, and Michael pasted a few patterns below for the SDK and error handling. We'll cover the rest on the 11/26 call.

1) Tool definitions: attached PDF includes a recommended JSON Schema template for tool definitions (inputs, outputs, validation, and idempotency). Example: payments.execute with fields {amount, currency, beneficiary_id, idempotency_key} and an explicit error schema for payment_rejected / payment_network_error. You can reuse the schema as-is or version it per tenant.

2) Parallel tools & partial failures: recommended pattern is "best-effort parallelism with deterministic fallback": 
- Invoke enrichment (embedding lookup + reranker) in parallel to the payments call where possible.
- Payments call is executed in the critical path; enrichment is best-effort. If enrichment fails or times out, return the payments result immediately with an enrichment status flag in the structured response (e.g., enrichment: {status: "partial", error_code: "emb_timeout"}).
- For downstream consistency, push enrichment results to an async store and emit an event so the UI can surface updates when enrichment becomes available.
- Retries: enrichment retries are controlled separately (backoff + max attempts) to avoid impacting payment latency.

3) Auth & short-lived creds: SDK supports OAuth on-behalf-of-user. Recommended flow: 
- Use your IdP to exchange an initial OAuth token for a short-lived Redwood token via a server-to-server exchange.
- Redwood issues short-lived session tokens scoped to the specific tool namespace and tenant; tokens are bound to a JWK for auditability.
- All tool calls are logged to the audit stream (we can push logs to your S3 / SIEM).

Michael — can you paste the SDK snippet for tool-call definition + error handling patterns we discussed?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hey James — quick patterns and example payloads. We'll walk through these on Thursday but wanted to drop the concrete snippets now so your team can review.

SDK / Tool-definition pattern (JSON Schema snippet):
- tool.name: payments.execute
- input_schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"amount":{"type":"number"},"currency":{"type":"string"},"beneficiary_id":{"type":"string"},"idempotency_key":{"type":"string"}},"required":["amount","currency","beneficiary_id","idempotency_key"]} 
- output_schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"string"},"transaction_id":{"type":"string"},"error_code":{"type":"string"}},"required":["status"]}

Parallel invocation pattern:
- Orchestrator invokes payments.execute and enrichment.lookup concurrently (async calls).
- Payments result is awaited with a short timeout window (e.g., 250ms) to meet p95 SLA.
- enrichment.lookup has longer timeout and its result is merged if available.

Structured response example (what the app receives):
{
  "payment": {"status":"success","transaction_id":"txn_12345"},
  "enrichment": {"status":"partial","error_code":"emb_timeout"}
}

Error handling and retries:
- Define explicit error taxonomy in tool defs: transient, permanent, auth, validation.
- For transient errors (network/timeouts) use exponential backoff with jitter, max 3 retries.
- For payments: do not auto-retry idempotent operations without client-supplied idempotency key.
- For enrichment: mark as best-effort; enqueue for async processing if it fails repeatedly.

Auth snippet (server-side exchange):
1) Client exchanges OIDC code with FinApps IdP -> returns user_token.
2) Server calls Redwood token-exchange endpoint with user_token -> returns short_lived_redwood_token scoped to payments.execute.
3) Calls to SDK include Authorization: Bearer short_lived_redwood_token and X-Redwood-Tenant header.

Attachments: redwood-tool-calling-patterns.pdf (contains full JSON schema, retry matrices, and a PoC checklist).
